title.official: Agreement on the Establishment of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization

issuer.name: Founding States of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization
Government of the People's Republic of China

relevance.reason: The constituent treaty of the first intergovernmental international organization specifically dedicated to artificial intelligence. It establishes WAICO as an independent intergovernmental organization with international legal personality, headquartered in Shanghai, with a Council and a Secretariat, and limits its functions exclusively to the civilian domain of AI (Article 3(2)). It is subject to ratification, acceptance or approval and enters into force on the deposit of the third such instrument (Article 15). It is a treaty, not a political declaration, and it is the second AI-specific treaty in the corpus alongside CETS 225.
ai_provisions: Article 1 — establishes WAICO as an independent intergovernmental international organization with international legal personality
Article 2 — purposes: human-centric AI, international cooperation, bridging the AI divide, risk mitigation and trustworthy AI

Article 3 — functions, including capacity building, alignment of governance rules and technical standards, open-source cooperation and support for the UN framework; functions are limited exclusively to the civilian domain
Article 4 — principles: UN Charter, sovereignty, diversity of civilizations, equality, multilateralism and extensive consultation
Articles 5–8 — Council, decision-making, Secretariat and financing
Article 10 — membership open to all States; Founding Members are States that sign during the open-for-signature period

Article 11 — observer status for non-member States and intergovernmental organisations, subject to an application to the Secretariat and approval by the Council; observers may attend the plenary on invitation and have no vote
Article 14 — signature from 1 May to 31 July 2026; ratification, acceptance or approval; accession thereafter
Article 15 — entry into force on the third instrument of ratification, acceptance or approval
Article 18 — China as depositary; Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish texts equally authentic
relevance.excluded_scope: Military AI is excluded: Article 3(2) limits the Organization's functions exclusively to the civilian domain. The Agreement establishes an organization and a cooperation framework; it does not itself set product rules, prohibitions, testing standards or a judicial dispute-settlement mechanism. Disputes are to be settled by consultation (Article 13).

dates.notes: Signed at the Shanghai ceremony on 16 July 2026. The Agreement was open for signature from 1 May to 31 July 2026. China's National People's Congress Standing Committee approved ratification on 6 November 2026; the deposit of the instrument of ratification and any depositary notification of entry into force were not verified. Article 18 designates the Government of the People's Republic of China as depositary; no public depositary status table or notification was located.

status_note: Treaty, binding on States that become parties, but not in force as of 23 November 2026. Article 15 requires three instruments of ratification, acceptance or approval for entry into force. China's National People's Congress approved ratification on 6 November 2026; no deposited instrument was verified, so the record does not count a ratification and the map records signature only. China's MFA reports 38 founding members, but the primary signing records individually identify 37: 29 States at the 16 July 2026 ceremony and eight later signatories named on 30–31 July 2026. The October 2026 progress report says nine States joined after the initial 29; eight are named, so one of the nine remains unnamed. Bangladesh is not that member: on 1 August 2026 its Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that Bangladesh would join "initially as an observer", after the signature period had closed. Article 11 requires an observer application and approval by the Council, and no admission is recorded; observers are not Founding Members under Article 10. Singapore has been reported as considering an invitation to join; it is a Pax Silica signatory and not a WAICO member. The discrepancy is recorded, not resolved. The Government of China is the depositary under Article 18; no public depositary register or notification of a deposited ratification was located.

parties.summary: 38 founding members reported by China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; 37 individually identified in the signing records: 29 States at the 16 July 2026 ceremony and eight later signatories named on 30–31 July 2026. The October 2026 progress report says nine States joined after the initial 29, so one of the nine remains unnamed. Bangladesh announced on 1 August 2026 that it would join 'initially as an observer', not as a founding member; Article 11 requires an observer application and Council approval, and no admission is recorded. Singapore has been reported as considering an invitation and is not a member. China's NPC approved ratification on 6 November 2026, but no deposit was verified.

notes: Approved by the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress on 6 November 2026.
Deposit of the instrument of ratification was not verified; no ratification is counted.

unknowns: The MFA reports 38 founding members as of 9 November 2026, but the signing records individually identify 37. The October 2026 progress report says nine States joined after the initial 29; eight are named in the 31 July account, so one of the nine - the 38th member - is not named in the MFA statements, the progress report or the Indonesian government's list of the 29 initial signatories. Bangladesh is not that member: it announced on 1 August 2026 that it would join 'initially as an observer', and Article 11 requires an observer application and Council approval; no admission is recorded. Singapore has been reported as considering an invitation and is not a member.

China is the depositary under Article 18. No public depositary register, status table or notification of signatures, ratifications or entry into force was located in the Chinese treaty database or MFA pages. The count of deposited ratifications is therefore 0, notwithstanding China's national approval on 6 November 2026.
The Agreement remains open to accession after 31 July 2026 (Article 14(3)); later accessions are not Founding Members and are not included in this list.
The exact date on which the MFA's 38-country count was reached is not stated; the October 2026 progress report already gives 38.

languages.note: Article 18: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish texts are equally authentic. Only the English reproduction of the Agreement was read; no official deposited text was acquired.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
sources.note: Official English account of the 16 July 2026 signing ceremony. States that WAICO is an independent intergovernmental international organization headquartered in Shanghai, that the Agreement follows the purposes of the UN Charter, and that representatives of 29 countries signed and became founding members.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
sources.note: Spokesperson Guo Jiakun, 9 November 2026: 38 countries became founding members; China was the first to approve the Agreement. The statement does not list the 38.

Xinhua report of 6 November 2026 on the closing meeting of the 25th session of the 14th NPC Standing Committee, which voted to ratify the Agreement on establishing WAICO. The NPC's own page could not be opened because its TLS configuration is unsupported by current browsers; this official report is used for the date and decision, and is not a depositary record of ratification.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China / Global AI Innovation Governance Center

The 31 July MFA account names eight of them; one of the nine remains unnamed.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
sources.note: Official account of 31 July 2026 naming the eight additional signatories: Brunei, Togo, Iran, Sudan, Vietnam, Georgia, Tanzania and Dominica (Dominica signed on 30 July).

sources.note: Report of 9 September 2026: Singapore's Minister for Digital Development and Information told Parliament that Singapore is considering an invitation to join WAICO and that there is no ASEAN position on either WAICO or Pax Silica. Reproduction of the Agreement text. Articles 1, 3, 10, 14, 15 and 18 were read. The depositary's official text was not located; the reproduction is used for the legal analysis, not as a substitute for the official text.

checks.check: Signing ceremony and legal nature checked on the official MFA English page.
checks.result: WAICO is described as an independent intergovernmental international organization headquartered in Shanghai; 29 countries signed the Agreement at the 16 July 2026 ceremony.

checks.check: Founding membership checked against the Indonesian government list and the MFA's later statements.
checks.result: 29 initial signatories are individually identified; the October 2026 progress report says nine more signed, and the 31 July 2026 MFA account names eight of them. The MFA reports 38 founding members, leaving one of the nine later signatories unnamed.

checks.check: Entry-into-force rule checked against the Agreement text and China's ratification decision.
checks.result: Article 15 requires three instruments of ratification, acceptance or approval. China's NPC approved ratification on 6 November 2026, but no deposited ratification or entry-into-force notification was verified.

checks.check: Treaty text checked against a reproduction and cross-checked with official descriptions.
checks.result: Articles 1, 3(2), 10, 14, 15 and 18 confirm the organization's legal personality, civilian-domain limitation, membership, signature/accession, entry into force and depositary. The official deposited text was not acquired.

checks.check: The 38th founding member checked against the Bangladesh and Singapore records.
checks.result: Bangladesh announced on 1 August 2026 that it would join 'initially as an observer', not as a founding member. Article 11 requires an observer application and Council approval, and no admission is recorded. Singapore was reported on 9 September 2026 as considering an invitation; it is a Pax Silica signatory and not a WAICO member. Neither closes the 37/38 gap.

checks.check: Depositary status rechecked for the 38th founding member and China's instrument of ratification.
checks.result: Article 18 designates the Government of the People's Republic of China as depositary. No public depositary register or status table for the Agreement, and no notification of a deposited Chinese instrument, was located in the Chinese treaty database or MFA pages. The 9 November 2026 MFA statement reports 38 founding members and says China was the first to approve the Agreement, but does not name the 38th or state that an instrument was deposited. The counts remain 38 reported, 37 identified and 0 deposited ratifications.

verification.notes: Metadata verified from official Chinese and Indonesian government sources. The record is metadata-only: no full text is stored. The depositary is China under Article 18; a recheck found no public depositary register or notification. The 38th founding member and the deposit of China's instrument of ratification remain unverified and are recorded as unknowns rather than inferred. Bangladesh's observer announcement and Singapore's reported invitation are recorded separately and are not treated as membership.

related.note: China's 2023 Global AI Governance Initiative is the policy line that led to the proposal for WAICO; it is a unilateral non-binding document, whereas the WAICO Agreement is a treaty.
The other AI-specific treaty in the corpus. CETS 225 is a human-rights framework convention; WAICO is a constituent instrument of an intergovernmental organization. Neither is in force.
The US-led Pax Silica coalition is the counterpart architecture. Kazakhstan is a signatory of both the Pax Silica Declaration and the WAICO Agreement.

gaps: The Agreement is not in force: Article 15 requires three deposited ratifications, acceptances or approvals, and none was verified.
China's NPC approved ratification on 6 November 2026, but the deposit of the instrument and any depositary notification were not verified; no ratification is counted.

The MFA reports 38 founding members while the signing records individually identify 37; the 38th member is not named in the official sources located. Bangladesh is not the 38th member: it announced on 1 August 2026 that it would join 'initially as an observer', subject to Article 11 and Council approval.

Observer status is not a party status: Article 11 allows the Council to admit non-member States and intergovernmental organisations as observers, who may attend the plenary on invitation and have no vote. No Council admission of Bangladesh is recorded.
No public depositary register or status table for signatures, ratifications and accessions was located; Article 18 designates China as depositary.
The full official text was not acquired; the record is metadata-only and relies on a reproduction for the article analysis.
The Organization's functions are limited to the civilian domain; military AI is outside the Agreement.
The Council, Secretariat, rules of procedure, budget and implementing instruments do not yet exist or were not verified.

provenance.discovered_via: CSIS 2026 analysis of global AI governance cited WAICO; the record was opened after the official MFA signing and ratification sources were located.
